cards.claim: CANS polynomial with 12 matmuls outperforms standard Muon polynomial with same matmul count (4 iterations)
cards.conditions: NanoGPT training, Muon optimizer, test loss convergence
cards.effect: Better convergence (test loss reduction) with equal computational cost
cards.quote: We observe, that CANS polynomial requiring 12 matmuls (purple) outperforms Muon polynomial with the same number of matmuls (4 iterations, cyan).

cards.claim: Higher derivative of polynomial at zero improves Muon optimizer performance
cards.conditions: Muon optimizer applied to neural network training
cards.evidence: Empirical observation from NanoGPT experiments and development work
cards.quote: In addition, higher derivative of composition of polynomials at zero noticeably improves the performance.

cards.claim: Smaller singular value deviation bounds improve Muon performance on larger models
cards.conditions: GPT-2 medium size model, Muon optimizer
cards.effect: Better training performance for larger models
cards.evidence: Empirical observation from prior work (Cesista et al., 2025)
cards.quote: However, further investigation suggested that decreased deviation improves the performance for larger models, e.g. GPT-2 medium ( Cesista et al., 2025 ).

cards.claim: Tuned Newton-Schulz coefficients converge faster than classical Newton-Schulz iteration
cards.conditions: Matrix orthogonalization problem with random normal entries, exact singular value bounds known
cards.effect: Fewer matmuls required for same convergence accuracy
cards.evidence: Figure 2 convergence comparison showing CANS requires fewer matmuls than classical NS
cards.quote: We conclude that the iterations with tuned coefficients converge noticeably faster than the classical Newton-Schulz (matmuls are proportional to time, see Table 3).

cards.claim: 5 fifth-order or 7 third-order polynomial compositions achieve higher derivative at zero than original Muon with no additional matmuls
cards.conditions: Muon optimizer, deviation tolerance ε specified, polynomial composition
cards.effect: Higher derivative at zero while maintaining same computational budget
cards.evidence: Figure 3 polynomial comparison and derivative analysis
cards.quote: Both polynomials have higher derivative at zero than original Muon polynomial, while requiring no more matmuls.

cards.claim: ε-orthogonalization (inexact orthogonalization) accelerates convergence without requiring exact singular value bounds
cards.conditions: Matrix orthogonalization with unknown smallest singular value, tolerance ε specified
cards.effect: Faster convergence to target accuracy even without singular value information
cards.evidence: Algorithm 2, Figure 2 dash-dotted lines showing ε-orthogonalization performance
cards.quote: ε-orthogonalization helps to accelerate the convergence of the algorithm, even if the smallest singular value is not available.

cards.claim: 9 third-order polynomial compositions achieve higher derivative than computational search methods without extra matmuls
cards.conditions: Muon optimizer, deviation tolerance ε=0.01 and ε=0.001, comparison with Jiacheng (2024) search method
cards.effect: Higher derivative at zero relative to computational search baseline
cards.evidence: Figure 4 polynomial comparison, Appendix J coefficients
cards.quote: Compositions of 9 3-rd order polynomials for (purple) and (blue) (Figure 4 ) also have higher derivatives than ( Jiacheng, 2024 ) polynomial found by computational search.
